article_title: Literature review of teaching skills programs for junior medical officers.
citation: Dannaway Jasan, Ng Heryanto, Schoo Adrian. (2016). Literature review of teaching skills programs for junior medical officers. International Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5685.14da
title: JMO teaching skills programs: predominantly workshop-based interventions using mixed instructional methods on adult learning, feedback and evaluation content
description: The reviewed programs are structured teaching interventions for junior medical officers, mostly workshops ranging from 1.5 hours to 1.5 days, delivered singly or as series over time. Instructional methods were typically mixed, "including role-play, brainstorming, reflection, and small-group discussion", with variants such as weekly email-delivered statements and direct supervision. Common content topics included adult learning principles, feedback, reflection, curriculum orientation, and evaluation; some programs used stakeholder panels or existing curricula such as the BEST curriculum.
requirements: Programs must be structured, detailing the teaching method and content, per the review's inclusion criteria
constraints: All but one included study was based in North America, limiting generalisability
target_learners: junior medical officers (residents), postgraduate years 1 to 5
target_learning_goals: teaching skills, feedback, adult learning principles, evaluation
examples: Pernar et al. delivered 29 brief statements on good teaching via weekly email over a year; Daniels-Brady et al. used weekly one-on-one meetings with the program director
key_sources: Dannaway Jasan, Ng Heryanto, Schoo Adrian. (2016). Literature review of teaching skills programs for junior medical officers. International Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5685.14da
